novelty_flags.label: thm:anytime-qte-coverage
novelty_flags.one_line: MineiroHoward2023 already covers the importance-weighted running conditional CDF whose deterministic-potential-outcome specialization is F_{a,t}; armwise inversion and subtraction give the asserted anytime QTE band.

novelty_flags.label: thm:anytime-qte-coverage and related_work
novelty_flags.one_line: The core attributes coverage to MineiroHoward2023 Theorem 3.4 and calls absence of an off-policy regression nuisance a strict simplification, but Theorem 3.1 supplies coverage, Theorem 3.4 is a smoothness-conditional width result, and the paper's importance-weighted construction itself uses only (W_t,X_t).

soundness_flags.label: ass:bounded-fixed-outcomes
soundness_flags.one_line: The cited DaiGraduHarshaw2023 source does not support the displayed uniform sup-norm condition: its Assumption 1 imposes bounded second/fourth prefix moments, while Definition 1 defines the Neyman ratio.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 3, Theorem 3.1 and equations (4)-(5); p. 5, Section 3.4 and Theorem 3.4
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper defines the averaged conditional CDF and its importance-weighted analogue, obtains time/value-uniform coverage through Theorem 3.1, and gives Theorem 3.4 only as a smoothness-conditional width bound for Algorithms 1-2.
Assumption 1 bounds prefix second and fourth moments and correlation; Definition 1 defines the Neyman ratio. Neither is the core's uniform condition sup_i,a |Y_i(a)|<=M.
The paper gives a time-uniform empirical-process finite-LIL bound and a quantile-uniform confidence sequence in the classical i.i.d. on-policy setting.
The published paper concerns design-based sequential ATE estimation and reports anytime near-logarithmic scalar Neyman regret, not QTE inference or a width-regret Pareto frontier.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Econometrics 249, Part A, 2025, Article 105857
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article develops fully adaptive and multistage covariate-adjusted response-adaptive designs for QTE estimation and states attainment of a semiparametric optimal variance lower bound.
The paper clips an arbitrary adaptive assignment policy to [1/k_t,1-1/k_t], so a fixed k_t=1/epsilon is the stated fixed-overlap specialization when epsilon<1/2.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Demote the CDF-to-QTE coverage result to an explicitly cited corollary of MineiroHoward2023 Theorem 3.1, correct the Theorem 3.4 and nuisance-language comparison, and retain only any genuinely new finite-population sharpness or constant claim as a root result.

Replace the Dai citation for uniform bounded potential outcomes with a source that actually states a sup-norm bounded design-based condition, or retag it as a separately justified standard boundedness restriction.

Make the field kernel staged and falsifiable: prove a finite m-quantile frontier with an observable primal-dual attaining rule and an approximation bound as m grows, before claiming continuum attainment over all q in I.

Upgrade the Halton slice from a single worked calculation to a generic nondegenerate incompatibility theorem over a stated class of marginal density pairs, with LiLuoWangFeng2025 and a scalar Neyman-regret comparator as explicit limiting cases.
